precepts.text: When ye come into the land, the land shall keep a sabbath unto the Lord.
precepts.point: The Sabbath of the land is built on the seventh-day Sabbath.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
Exodus 23 gives the seventh year release: work the land six years, “But the seventh year thou shalt let it rest and lie still; that the poor of thy people may eat”. Leviticus 25 lays out the same law: “And the Lord spake unto Moses in mount Sinai, saying, Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When ye come into the land which I give you, then shall the land keep a sabbath unto the Lord”. He is telling us what to do when we enter the land, and we entered the land under Joshua, not under Moses.

“Six years thou shalt sow thy field, and six years thou shalt prune thy vineyard, and gather in the fruit thereof; But in the seventh year shall be a sabbath of rest unto the land”. Don't farm the land that year. “That which groweth of its own accord of thy harvest thou shalt not reap”: whatever grows on its own during the seventh year, that is what you eat. “And the sabbath of the land shall be meat for you; for thee, and for thy servant, and for thy maid, and for thy hired servant, and for thy stranger that sojourneth with thee”.

The seventh year release is built on the seventh-day Sabbath. Exodus 23 says it right after the land: “Six days thou shalt do thy work, and on the seventh day thou shalt rest”. The Sabbath goes for the land as well; when you have property, you let your land rest.

And the question everybody asks is answered in verse 20: “What shall we eat the seventh year? behold, we shall not sow, nor gather in our increase: Then I will command my blessing upon you in the sixth year, and it shall bring forth fruit for three years”. The sixth year covers you for three years. Brothers and sisters say, I got to work on the Sabbath because that's my money day. Then you don't believe what we just read. That was the same question in verse 20, and God answered it: work six, rest on the seventh, and he provides.

precepts.text: Behold, I send an Angel before thee, to keep thee in the way; obey his voice, provoke him not; for he will not pardon your transgressions: for my name is in him.
precepts.point: The same angel went before Israel out of Egypt: Behold, I send an Angel before thee; beware of him, and obey his voice, provoke him not, for my name is in him.

note.label: Exodus 3: The Angel in the Burning Bush

precepts.why:
The same angel that appeared in the bush went before Israel out of Egypt. “Behold, I send an Angel before thee, to keep thee in the way, and to bring thee into the place which I have prepared. Beware of him, and obey his voice, provoke him not; for he will not pardon your transgressions: for my name is in him.”

My name is in him: the Most High's name is in that Angel, which is why the voice out of the bush could say, “I am the God of thy father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.” If Israel obeyed his voice, the Lord would be “an enemy unto thine enemies”, and “mine Angel shall go before thee, and bring thee in unto the Amorites, and the Hittites, and the Perizzites, and the Canaanites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites: and I will cut them off.” That Angel, by whose hand Moses was sent as a ruler and a deliverer, is Christ.

precepts.text: Enter not into the path of the wicked; they sleep not except they have done mischief, and they drink the wine of violence.
precepts.point: Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil. Enter not into the path of the wicked; sinners entice, saying come with us, cast in thy lot among us, but walk not thou in the way with them, for their feet run to evil and make haste to shed blood. Many of our young men's lives end short because they follow a multitude to do evil. To be in the midst of the singing, like the whole school hollering fight, fight, fight, is to be in the multitude the Most High warns of; a soul without knowledge of the laws of God hastes with his feet and sins.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil”. Proverbs says the same: “Enter not into the path of the wicked, and go not in the way of evil men. Avoid it, pass not by it, turn from it, and pass away.”

Why: “For they sleep not, except they have done mischief; and their sleep is taken away, unless they cause some to fall. For they eat the bread of wickedness, and drink the wine of violence.” The multitude that does evil cannot rest until it has done mischief and caused some to fall. Do not go in the way with them.

precepts.text: If sinners entice thee, consent thou not; walk not thou in the way with them, for their feet run to evil.

To be in the midst of the singing, like the whole school hollering fight, fight, fight, is to be in the multitude the Most High warns of; a soul without knowledge of the laws of God hastes with his feet and sins.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

precepts.why:
“My son, if sinners entice thee, consent thou not.” The multitude entices: “If they say, Come with us, let us lay wait for blood, let us lurk privily for the innocent without cause: Let us swallow them up alive as the grave; and whole, as those that go down into the pit: We shall find all precious substance, we shall fill our houses with spoil: Cast in thy lot among us; let us all have one purse”.

The answer is the law of Exodus 23: “My son, walk not thou in the way with them; refrain thy foot from their path”. Their feet run to evil and make haste to shed blood. Many of our young men’s lives end short because they follow a multitude to do evil.

precepts.why:
Isaiah describes the multitude that does evil: “Their webs shall not become garments, neither shall they cover themselves with their works: their works are works of iniquity, and the act of violence is in their hands.”

“Their feet run to evil, and they make haste to shed innocent blood: their thoughts are thoughts of iniquity; wasting and destruction are in their paths.” That is the way the sinners of Proverbs 1 call you into, and the path Proverbs 4 says to turn from. Their feet run to evil, so refrain thy foot from their path.

precepts.text: Ye shall not be afraid of the face of man, for the judgment is God's.
precepts.point: Neither shalt thou speak in a cause to decline after many to wrest judgment: once the judgment has been passed by the leaders, do not speak out against it to sway people's opinion in a different direction. The judgment is God's; whoever sits in leadership, at the end of the day it comes from the Most High, so to sway people against it is to go against God. When a Romans 16:17 marking is put out in your congregation, follow it, because it ultimately comes from God.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not raise a false report: put not thine hand with the wicked to be an unrighteous witness.” Basically, thou shalt not lie. If you did not see it, do not make up a story like you were there; keep your mouth shut.

And “neither shalt thou speak in a cause to decline after many to wrest judgment”: once the judgment has been passed by the leaders, do not speak out against it to sway people’s opinion in a different direction. The judges were charged, “Ye shall not respect persons in judgment; but ye shall hear the small as well as the great; ye shall not be afraid of the face of man; for the judgment is God’s”.

The judgment is God’s. Whoever sits in leadership, at the end of the day it comes from the Most High, so to sway people against it is to go against God.

precepts.text: Judge righteously between every man and his brother; ye shall not respect persons in judgment, but hear the small as well as the great.
precepts.point: In this corrupt system in Babylon, how innocent or guilty you come out depends on how much lawyer you can afford. Our law was holy and righteous because none of that made a difference: either you were right or you were wrong, whether poor or rich. The Pharisees learned the ways of the heathen and began respecting persons, which the book of James speaks against.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

precepts.why:
“Neither shalt thou countenance a poor man in his cause.” This deals with judgment: do not be a respecter of persons because a man is poor, as if he is automatically wrong when he brings a matter against a rich man. The judges were charged, “Hear the causes between your brethren, and judge righteously between every man and his brother, and the stranger that is with him. Ye shall not respect persons in judgment; but ye shall hear the small as well as the great; ye shall not be afraid of the face of man; for the judgment is God’s”.

In this corrupt system in Babylon, how innocent or guilty you come out depends on how much lawyer you can afford. Our law was holy and righteous because none of that made a difference: either you were right or you were wrong, whether poor or rich. The small was heard as well as the great.

The Pharisees learned the ways of the heathen and began respecting persons, which the book of James speaks against.

precepts.text: Thou shalt not see thy brother's ox go astray and hide thyself; in any case bring it again to thy brother, even a brother thou knowest not, and help him lift his ass or his ox when it is fallen.
precepts.point: Deuteronomy means the second law; it speaks the law plain in case you did not understand it here. Keep Deuteronomy 22:1-4 and Leviticus 19:17-18 in your hip pocket with this verse.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

precepts.why:
Deuteronomy says the same law with thy brother in the place of thine enemy: “Thou shalt not see thy brother’s ox or his sheep go astray, and hide thyself from them: thou shalt in any case bring them again unto thy brother.” In any case, no matter how you feel about him. So the enemy that hates you in Exodus 23 is your brother, your own nation.

“And if thy brother be not nigh unto thee, or if thou know him not, then thou shalt bring it unto thine own house, and it shall be with thee until thy brother seek after it, and thou shalt restore it to him again.” He is still your brother even if you never grew up with him. The same for “his ass”, “his raiment”, “and with all lost thing of thy brother’s, which he hath lost, and thou hast found”. And the ass under his burden: “Thou shalt not see thy brother’s ass or his ox fall down by the way, and hide thyself from them: thou shalt surely help him to lift them up again.”

Deuteronomy means the second law; it speaks the law plain in case you did not understand it here. That is real love for your own people. Keep Deuteronomy 22:1-4 in your hip pocket with this verse.

precepts.text: Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart, nor bear grudge against the children of thy people, but love thy neighbour as thyself.
precepts.point: Deuteronomy means the second law; it speaks the law plain in case you did not understand it here. Keep Deuteronomy 22:1-4 and Leviticus 19:17-18 in your hip pocket with this verse.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him. Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am the Lord.”

The enemy and “him that hateth thee” in Exodus 23 are among the children of thy people. You do not hate him in your heart, you do not avenge or bear a grudge against him; you bring his ox back and help his ass up, because you love your neighbour as yourself. Keep Leviticus 19:17-18 in your hip pocket with this verse.

precepts.text: Love your enemies: read with Exodus 23:4-5 and Deuteronomy 22:1-4, the enemy to be loved and helped is the brother of thine own nation that hates thee.
precepts.point: Deuteronomy means the second law; it speaks the law plain in case you did not understand it here. Keep Deuteronomy 22:1-4 and Leviticus 19:17-18 in your hip pocket with this verse.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

precepts.why:
“But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you”.

Matthew 5:44 is misconstrued to mean the other nations. Read it with Exodus 23:4-5 and Deuteronomy 22:1-4: the enemy to be loved, the one that hates you whom you do good to, is the brother of thine own nation that hates thee. Bringing back his ox and helping with his ass is doing good to them that hate you.

precepts.text: Christ said, If I by Beelzebub cast out devils, by whom do your children cast them out? He mentioned the name of another god and did no sin.
precepts.point: Joshua and Deuteronomy double it: neither make mention of the name of their gods, nor cause to swear by them, neither serve them, nor bow yourselves unto them; and if thy brother or son or wife entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, thou shalt not consent. Wherever you are, do not go trying to find out how the nations worship their gods.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

precepts.why:
To “make no mention of the name of other gods” is not saying you cannot pronounce the names Buddha, Allah, Krishna, Ra. Christ himself said, “And if I by Beelzebub cast out devils, by whom do your children cast them out? therefore they shall be your judges.” Beelzebub is the chief of the devils, a name derived from the Philistine god of Ekron. Christ named him, and Christ did no sin; so the verse cannot mean the bare saying of a name.

The Lord says this same thing three ways in this one chapter, and the other two places show the meaning: in verse 24, thou shalt not bow down to their gods nor serve them nor do after their works; and in verses 32 and 33, thou shalt make no covenant with them nor with their gods, for if thou serve their gods it will surely be a snare unto thee. Make no mention means do not learn how to serve and worship them.

precepts.text: Neither make mention of the name of their gods, nor cause to swear by them, neither serve them, nor bow yourselves unto them, but cleave unto the Lord your God.
precepts.point: Joshua and Deuteronomy double it: neither make mention of the name of their gods, nor cause to swear by them, neither serve them, nor bow yourselves unto them; and if thy brother or son or wife entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, thou shalt not consent. Wherever you are, do not go trying to find out how the nations worship their gods.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

precepts.why:
Joshua doubles it: “Be ye therefore very courageous to keep and to do all that is written in the book of the law of Moses, that ye turn not aside therefrom to the right hand or to the left; That ye come not among these nations, these that remain among you; neither make mention of the name of their gods, nor cause to swear by them, neither serve them, nor bow yourselves unto them: But cleave unto the Lord your God, as ye have done unto this day.”

Making mention of the name of their gods is set right alongside swearing by them, serving them and bowing to them. It is the worship that is forbidden. Do not come among the nations to learn their gods; cleave unto the Lord your God.

precepts.text: If thy nearest kin entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, thou shalt not consent unto him nor hearken unto him.
precepts.point: Joshua and Deuteronomy double it: neither make mention of the name of their gods, nor cause to swear by them, neither serve them, nor bow yourselves unto them; and if thy brother or son or wife entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, thou shalt not consent. Wherever you are, do not go trying to find out how the nations worship their gods.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

precepts.why:
“If thy brother, the son of thy mother, or thy son, or thy daughter, or the wife of thy bosom, or thy friend, which is as thine own soul, entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, which thou hast not known, thou, nor thy fathers”, whether their gods be “nigh unto thee, or far off from thee, from the one end of the earth even unto the other end of the earth; Thou shalt not consent unto him, nor hearken unto him; neither shall thine eye pity him, neither shalt thou spare, neither shalt thou conceal him”.

That is what making mention of other gods means: going to serve them. Not even your nearest kin can entice you to it. Wherever you are, from one end of the earth to the other, do not go trying to find out how the nations worship their gods.

precepts.text: The feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover; the two names are one feast.
precepts.point: The feast of harvest, the firstfruits of thy labours, is also known as Pentecost and the feast of weeks; and the feast of ingathering, in the end of the year, is also known as the feast of tabernacles and the feast of booths.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

precepts.why:
“Three times thou shalt keep a feast unto me in the year.” The first is “the feast of unleavened bread”, kept “in the time appointed of the month Abib”, the first month of the year. That feast is the Passover, as it is written: “Now the feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover.” The two names are one feast.

“and none shall appear before me empty”: you could not come empty-handed. You brought the tenth of your oil, your wine, whatever was required, for the priests to replenish the storehouses.

Next, “the feast of harvest, the firstfruits of thy labours” is also known as Pentecost and the feast of weeks; and “the feast of ingathering, which is in the end of the year” is also known as the feast of tabernacles and the feast of booths. At these three feasts all the males appeared before the Lord God.

precepts.text: An angel went before Israel to keep them in the way; obey his voice and provoke him not, and the Lord will be an enemy unto thine enemies and cut off the nations.
precepts.point: If Israel obeyed the angel's voice, the Lord would be an enemy unto their enemies and cut off the nations of the land before them. The scripture makes a distinction: the enemy whose ox or ass you must bring back and help is your brother that hates you, as the parallel law shows by using the word brother; the enemies of the nations are those the Most High said He would cut off. So love thine enemies does not mean the nation Israel was sold to; it speaks of your brother that you may be at odds with.

note.label: Exodus 40: The Tabernacle Reared Up and the Glory of the Lord

precepts.why:
“Behold, I send an Angel before thee, to keep thee in the way, and to bring thee into the place which I have prepared. Beware of him, and obey his voice, provoke him not; for he will not pardon your transgressions: for my name is in him.” The cloud by day and the fire by night that led the house of Israel in all their journeys go with this Angel sent before them.

That shows why the first generation did not make it to the promised land. They provoked the angel, transgressed, complained, worshipped idols and wanted to go back into Egypt, and he will not pardon your transgressions.

“But if thou shalt indeed obey his voice, and do all that I speak; then I will be an enemy unto thine enemies, and an adversary unto thine adversaries.” The Angel would bring them in unto the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hivites and the Jebusites, “and I will cut them off.” Those are the enemies of the nations, whom the Most High said He would cut off.

precepts.text: Bring back thine enemy's ox going astray and help him that hateth thee; this enemy is your brother.
precepts.point: If Israel obeyed the angel's voice, the Lord would be an enemy unto their enemies and cut off the nations of the land before them. The scripture makes a distinction: the enemy whose ox or ass you must bring back and help is your brother that hates you, as the parallel law shows by using the word brother; the enemies of the nations are those the Most High said He would cut off. So love thine enemies does not mean the nation Israel was sold to; it speaks of your brother that you may be at odds with.

note.label: Exodus 40: The Tabernacle Reared Up and the Glory of the Lord

precepts.why:
“If thou meet thine enemy’s ox or his ass going astray, thou shalt surely bring it back to him again. If thou see the ass of him that hateth thee lying under his burden, and wouldest forbear to help him, thou shalt surely help with him.”

The scripture makes a distinction. This enemy, whose ox or ass you must bring back and whom you must help, is your brother that hates you. In the same chapter the Lord promises to be an enemy unto Israel's enemies and to cut off the nations of the land; those enemies are not the ones whose ox you bring back.

precepts.text: Do not do after the works of the heathen; serve the Lord, and he shall bless thy bread and thy water and take sickness away from the midst of thee.
precepts.point: Serve the Lord and he shall bless thy bread and thy water, and take sickness away from the midst of thee: keep the dietary laws, what to eat and not eat, how to cook it and how to season it, and do not bow down to the gods of the heathen nor do after their works.

note.label: Leviticus 3: The Peace Offering Without Blemish

precepts.why:
The Lord brought Israel in unto the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, and said, “Thou shalt not bow down to their gods, nor serve them, nor do after their works”. Eating blood after the doings of Egypt is doing after the works of the heathen.

“And ye shall serve the Lord your God, and he shall bless thy bread, and thy water; and I will take sickness away from the midst of thee.” Keep the dietary laws, what to eat and not eat, how to cook it and how to season it, and do not bow down to the gods of the heathen nor do after their works; the blessing is on thy bread and thy water, and sickness taken away.

precepts.text: Obey His voice and He is an enemy to thine enemies; the nations of Canaan and their gods were to be overthrown, not learned from.
precepts.point: Coming out of Egypt required a transformed mind: not conformed to the way of life of Egypt or Canaan, but renewed to the commandments of the Most High.

note.label: Leviticus 18: After the Doings of Egypt and Canaan Shall Ye Not Do

precepts.why:
The land of Canaan was full of idols, and the Most High told Israel before they got there what to do about them. “if thou shalt indeed obey his voice, and do all that I speak; then I will be an enemy unto thine enemies, and an adversary unto thine adversaries.” His Angel would go before them and bring them in unto the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hivites and the Jebusites, and cut them off.

The charge in Canaan was plain: “Thou shalt not bow down to their gods, nor serve them, nor do after their works: but thou shalt utterly overthrow them, and quite break down their images.” The nations of Canaan and their gods were to be overthrown, not learned from. That is what “after the doings of the land of Canaan, whither I bring you, shall ye not do” means.

And the blessing for obeying: “ye shall serve the Lord your God, and he shall bless thy bread, and thy water; and I will take sickness away from the midst of thee.”

precepts.text: Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil; being enticed to serve other gods is evil, so follow them not.
precepts.point: This is why Leviticus 5:1 is opened at the start of class: if you know of anything, you are supposed to utter it. Many grew up on snitches get stitches, but in repentance we have to understand that concealing sin is part of why Israel is in the condition it is in, and we have to teach righteousness. It is that simple.

note.label: Deuteronomy 13: Enticers to Other Gods Put Away

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil; neither shalt thou speak in a cause to decline after many to wrest judgment”. Being enticed to serve other gods is evil, so follow them not. Whether it is a multitude, or the one closest to you, thy brother, thy son, thy daughter, the wife of thy bosom, or thy friend which is as thine own soul, saying “Let us go and serve other gods”, the answer is the same: “Thou shalt not consent unto him, nor hearken unto him”.

Nobody can make you do anything, but they can influence you. Following a multitude into evil or following the people nearest you into evil is still following, and the commandment is not to. Do not give anyone that credit and let them cause you to lose your crown.

precepts.text: I will not drive them out before thee in one year, but by little and little, until thou be increased and inherit the land.
precepts.point: The nations were also left among Israel to prove them, whether they would keep the commandments of the Most High, and so that the generations which had not known the wars of Canaan might be taught war. We all know what ended up happening with that proving, and it comes later on as we read.

note.label: Joshua 13: Much Land Yet to Be Possessed

precepts.why:
Joshua is old and stricken in years, “and there remaineth yet very much land to be possessed.” The Most High had already said how it would go: “I will not drive them out from before thee in one year; lest the land become desolate, and the beast of the field multiply against thee. By little and little I will drive them out from before thee, until thou be increased, and inherit the land.”

He was not going to drive out these nations in one year, but little and little as Israel increased, so much land still remained when Joshua was old.

precepts.text: I will send hornets before thee, which shall drive out the Hivite, the Canaanite, and the Hittite, from before thee.
precepts.point: I have given you a land for which ye did not labour, and cities which ye built not, and ye dwell in them; of the vineyards and oliveyards which ye planted not do ye eat. Israel took over everything the nations had in those lands, the ships, the vineyards, the merchandise, and became the merchants of the land; it was theirs, because it was promised.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

precepts.why:
“And I sent the hornet before you, which drave them out from before you, even the two kings of the Amorites; but not with thy sword, nor with thy bow.” This was promised long before: “And I will send hornets before thee, which shall drive out the Hivite, the Canaanite, and the Hittite, from before thee.”

God was doing the fighting. Great nations bigger and more than Israel fell because the Most High was with them, not because of Israel's sword or bow. And because it was promised, everything those nations had in the land, the cities, the vineyards and oliveyards, the ships and the merchandise, was Israel's to dwell in and eat of; Israel became the merchants of the land.

precepts.text: Thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor with their gods; they shall not dwell in thy land, lest they make thee sin against me.
precepts.point: Because Israel disobeyed, the sentence falls: I will not drive them out from before you, but they shall be as thorns in your sides, and their gods shall be a snare unto you. The people lifted up their voice and wept, called the place Bochim, and sacrificed there unto the Most High.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

precepts.why:
The angel rehearsed the command Israel broke: “ye shall make no league with the inhabitants of this land; ye shall throw down their altars: but ye have not obeyed my voice”. It was given from the beginning: “Thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor with their gods. They shall not dwell in thy land, lest they make thee sin against me: for if thou serve their gods, it will surely be a snare unto thee.” The Most High warned against letting them dwell in the land because they would make us sin against him, and he keeps reiterating that we will be snared and trapped by serving what these nations serve. Because Israel disobeyed, the sentence fell: “their gods shall be a snare unto you.”

The same is true today in the places where we are scattered: we have made leagues with the inhabitants of the land, and their gods are a snare to us.

precepts.text: The promise behind this history: the Most High sent an Angel before Israel, and we know that angel is Christ; obey his voice, and I will be an enemy unto thine enemies, for mine Angel shall go before thee and bring thee in unto the Amorites, and I will cut them off.
precepts.point: And the LORD God of Israel delivered Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and they smote them: so Israel possessed all the land of the Amorites, from Arnon even unto Jabbok, and from the wilderness even unto Jordan. That is how Israel got the land of the Amorites: the Lord gave it in battle when they came out against his people.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

precepts.why:
The promise behind this whole history. “Behold, I send an Angel before thee, to keep thee in the way, and to bring thee into the place which I have prepared.” We know that Angel is Christ: “for my name is in him.” “But if thou shalt indeed obey his voice, and do all that I speak; then I will be an enemy unto thine enemies, and an adversary unto thine adversaries. For mine Angel shall go before thee, and bring thee in unto the Amorites, and the Hittites, and the Perizzites, and the Canaanites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites: and I will cut them off.”

That is what happened with Sihon. Israel asked passage; Sihon gathered all his people, pitched in Jahaz and fought against Israel; and “the Lord God of Israel delivered Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel”. The Angel went before Israel and brought them in unto the Amorites, and the Lord cut them off, as he promised. Israel did nothing to Sihon; the Lord was an enemy to Israel’s enemies.

precepts.text: Thou shalt take no gift, for the gift blindeth the wise and perverteth the words of the righteous; that gift is what goes into bribes.
precepts.point: When Samuel was old he made his sons judges over Israel: Joel the firstborn and Abiah his second, judges in Beersheba. But his sons walked not in his ways; they turned aside after lucre, took bribes, and perverted judgment.

note.label: 1 Samuel 8: Give Us a King Like All the Nations

precepts.why:
“And thou shalt take no gift: for the gift blindeth the wise, and perverteth the words of the righteous.” That gift is what goes into bribes.

Samuel's sons Joel and Abiah, judges in Beer-sheba, broke this very law: they “walked not in his ways, but turned aside after lucre, and took bribes, and perverted judgment.” The gift perverted their judgment just as the law said it would.

We see that same thing going on now in this political climate, and even in the church system. This is why the churches will not teach us who we are or teach the commandments of the Most High; when riots and unrest break out, it is those same pastors who go out to calm the people down.

precepts.text: The innocent and righteous slay thou not; the law in the book that Saul was set on breaking.
precepts.point: Saul hearkened unto Jonathan and sware, As the Lord liveth, he shall not be slain; and Jonathan brought David back to Saul, and he was in his presence as in times past.

note.label: 1 Samuel 19: A Faithful Friend Is a Strong Defence

precepts.why:
“Keep thee far from a false matter; and the innocent and righteous slay thou not: for I will not justify the wicked.” That is the law in the book, and Saul was set on breaking it.

Jonathan put it before his father: “Let not the king sin against his servant, against David; because he hath not sinned against thee, and because his works have been to thee-ward very good.” David “did put his life in his hand, and slew the Philistine”, and Saul saw it “and didst rejoice.” So “wherefore then wilt thou sin against innocent blood, to slay David without a cause?”

Without a cause: in chapter 18 it was just a feeling, wrath at David for nothing. As Christ explained in the spirit, that anger without a cause leads to actually wanting to murder, which is why it carries the same judgment.

precepts.text: Three times in the year all thy males shall appear before the Lord, the same thing being said in Job.
precepts.point: So this is talking about the same thing; it is not just talking about angels alone.

note.label: Job 1: The Trial of an Upright Man

precepts.why:
“Three times in the year all thy males shall appear before the Lord God.” That is the same thing being said in Job: “there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord”.

So when it says “the sons of God”, this is talking about the line, the lineage of Adam. Before we were called Israelites we were called the sons of God, and even still today we are called the sons of the living God. It is not just talking about angels alone; it is the sons of God appearing before the Lord as the males of Israel were commanded to, and Satan came also among them.

precepts.text: Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil; there is a law set up for how we govern ourselves.
precepts.point: He asks the Lord not to let his heart be inclined to practice wicked works with men that work iniquity, and not to let him eat of their dainties, meaning not to partake or follow the wicked to do evil.

note.label: Psalm 141: A Prayer to Be Kept From Evil

precepts.why:
“Incline not my heart to any evil thing, to practise wicked works with men that work iniquity: and let me not eat of their dainties.” Not eating of their dainties means not partaking or following the wicked to do evil. “Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil; neither shalt thou speak in a cause to decline after many to wrest judgment”. There is a law set up for how we govern ourselves.

David also asks for a watch before his mouth and the door of his lips kept, help to control his mouth, the same as James telling us to bridle the tongue; and that his heart not be inclined to evil, that his mind and spirit not go after evil things but walk in the spirit.

precepts.text: Thou shalt take no gift, for the gift blinds the wise and perverts the words of the righteous.
precepts.point: There is no point in a fool holding a price to buy wisdom when he has no heart for it.

note.label: Proverbs 17: Trials That Refine and the Weight of Words

precepts.why:
“And thou shalt take no gift: for the gift blindeth the wise, and perverteth the words of the righteous.” The law says it twice, in Exodus and again in Deuteronomy: the gift blinds the wise and perverts the words of the righteous.

That is how the wicked come to be justified and the just condemned, the thing that is abomination to the Lord.

precepts.text: Bring back your enemy's ox or ass going astray, and help even the ass of him that hates you lying under his burden.
precepts.point: David showed this with Saul: he cut off the skirt of Saul's robe in the cave but would not kill the Most High's anointed, and Saul confessed David was more righteous, rewarding good for evil. The coals of fire are the shame that comes on such an enemy.

note.label: Proverbs 25: The Proverbs of Solomon Copied by Hezekiah's Men

precepts.why:
“If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink”. This is not talking about our natural enemies of the other nations. This is about an enemy among your own people.

The law says the same thing: “If thou meet thine enemy’s ox or his ass going astray, thou shalt surely bring it back to him again. If thou see the ass of him that hateth thee lying under his burden, and wouldest forbear to help him, thou shalt surely help with him.” Even your enemy's ox or ass going astray you bring back; even the ass of him that hates you, lying under his burden, you help. Bread and water for the hungry enemy is the same law.

These are commandments given only to Israel, to be taught to our children, so the enemy in view is one among your people. Do him good, and the Most High will reward you.

moments.label: Integrated but Divided: What Did We Lose?
Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free
Escape Thankskilling : Oh God & My Lord

points: And I will set thy bounds from the Red sea even unto the sea of the Philistines, and from the desert unto the river: for I will deliver the inhabitants of the land into your hand; and thou shalt drive them out before thee.

note.label: Integrated but Divided: What Did We Lose?

points: Thou shalt make no covenant with them. God said what? Thou shalt make no covenant with them. We should not make no covenant with that nation. Nor with their gods. Nor with what? With their gods.

note.label: Integrated but Divided: What Did We Lose?

points: They shall not dwell in thy land, lest they make thee sin against me: for if thou serve their gods, it will surely be a snare unto thee.

This is why I want segregation to come back. God said they should not live in your land. They are going to make you sin against me, and you are going to go worshipping their gods. That is what God said. I do not know about you. I do not want these animals near my house. I do not want them near me.

note.label: Integrated but Divided: What Did We Lose?

points: Six years sow the land, but the seventh let it rest and lie still.
The Sabbath of the land is built on the seventh-day Sabbath.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

points: Behold, I send an Angel before thee: the same angel that spoke to Moses out of the bush, to be obeyed and not provoked.

note.label: Escape Thankskilling : Oh God & My Lord

points: Thou shalt not raise a false report, nor put thine hand with the wicked to be an unrighteous witness: basically, thou shalt not lie. If you did not see it, do not make up a story like you were there; keep your mouth shut.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

points: Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil. Enter not into the path of the wicked; sinners entice, saying come with us, cast in thy lot among us, but walk not thou in the way with them, for their feet run to evil and make haste to shed blood. Many of our young men's lives end short because they follow a multitude to do evil. To be in the midst of the singing, like the whole school hollering fight, fight, fight, is to be in the multitude the Most High warns of; a soul without knowledge of the laws of God hastes with his feet and sins.

Neither shalt thou speak in a cause to decline after many to wrest judgment: once the judgment has been passed by the leaders, do not speak out against it to sway people's opinion in a different direction. The judgment is God's; whoever sits in leadership, at the end of the day it comes from the Most High, so to sway people against it is to go against God. When a Romans 16:17 marking is put out in your congregation, follow it, because it ultimately comes from God.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

points: Neither shalt thou countenance a poor man in his cause. This deals with judgment: do not be a respecter of persons because a man is poor, as if he is automatically wrong when he brings a matter against a rich man. The judges were charged to hear the small as well as the great.

In this corrupt system in Babylon, how innocent or guilty you come out depends on how much lawyer you can afford. Our law was holy and righteous because none of that made a difference: either you were right or you were wrong, whether poor or rich. The Pharisees learned the ways of the heathen and began respecting persons, which the book of James speaks against.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

points: If thou meet thine enemy's ox or his ass going astray, thou shalt surely bring it back to him again; if thou see the ass of him that hateth thee lying under his burden, thou shalt surely help with him. This enemy that hates you is your brother, your own nation, not the other nations as Matthew 5:44 is misconstrued to mean.

Deuteronomy 22:1-4 proves it, saying the same law with thy brother in the place of thine enemy: thou shalt not see thy brother's ox or sheep go astray; in any case, no matter how you feel, bring them again unto thy brother. And if thou know him not, keep it in thine own house until thy brother seek after it. He is still your brother even if you never grew up with him; that is real love for your own people.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

points: Thou shalt not wrest the judgment of thy poor in his cause: verse six explains verse three again in case you did not catch it, do not be partial in judgment.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

points: Keep thee far from a false matter; the innocent and righteous slay thou not, for the Most High will not justify the wicked.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

points: Thou shalt take no gift, for the gift blindeth the wise and perverteth the words of the righteous: do not take a bribe when it comes to judgment; be upright and honest.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

points: Also thou shalt not oppress a stranger, for ye know the heart of a stranger, seeing ye were strangers in the land of Egypt. This is speaking about us, as Exodus 22:21 already laid out with Leviticus 25:35.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

points: The seventh year ties into the count of the jubilee: seven sabbaths of years to the forty-ninth year, and in the fiftieth year no plowing of the land, which the law takes up later.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

points: Six years thou shalt sow thy land, but the seventh year thou shalt let it rest and lie still, that the poor of thy people may eat, and the beasts of the field after them; likewise the vineyard and the oliveyard. That is mercy from the Lord: in the seventh year the land itself fed the poor.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

points: Six days do thy work, and on the seventh day rest, that thine ox and thine ass may rest, and the son of thy handmaid and the stranger may be refreshed. The stranger here can be another nation working for you: they too get their due rest on the sabbath.

When the Lord sets Israel back up to rule, the nations will kick and scream at first, but once these laws are applied there will be righteousness reigning over the earth like they have never seen, and all will be refreshed on the sabbath, spiritually and physically.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

points: Make no mention of the name of other gods is not saying you cannot pronounce the names Buddha, Allah, Krishna, Ra. Christ himself named Beelzebub, the chief of the devils, a name derived from the Philistine god of Ekron, and Christ did no sin; so the verse cannot mean the bare saying of a name.

The Lord says this same thing three ways in this one chapter, and the other two places show the meaning: verse 24, thou shalt not bow down to their gods nor serve them nor do after their works; and verses 32 and 33, thou shalt make no covenant with them nor with their gods, for if thou serve their gods it will surely be a snare unto thee. Make no mention means do not learn how to serve and worship them.

Joshua and Deuteronomy double it: neither make mention of the name of their gods, nor cause to swear by them, neither serve them, nor bow yourselves unto them; and if thy brother or son or wife entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, thou shalt not consent. Wherever you are, do not go trying to find out how the nations worship their gods.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

points: The feast of unleavened bread is the Passover, kept in the time appointed of the month Abib, the first month of the year, as it is written, the feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover.
None shall appear before me empty: you could not come empty-handed. You brought the tenth of your oil, your wine, whatever was required, for the priests to replenish the storehouses.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

points: The feast of harvest, the firstfruits of thy labours, is also known as Pentecost and the feast of weeks; and the feast of ingathering, in the end of the year, is also known as the feast of tabernacles and the feast of booths.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

points: Three times thou shalt keep a feast unto me in the year: all the males appeared before the Lord God three times in the year.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

points: Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread, neither shall the fat of my sacrifice remain until the morning. The first of the firstfruits of thy land thou shalt bring into the house of the Lord thy God.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

points: Thou shalt not seethe a kid in his mother's milk: the Lord repeats what was read at Exodus 22:30, that the young one was not to be taken too young and too soon; it stayed its seven days with his dam before it was given.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

points: Behold, I send an Angel before thee, to keep thee in the way and to bring thee into the place which I have prepared. Beware of him, obey his voice, provoke him not, for he will not pardon your transgressions: for my name is in him. That Angel is speaking of Christ.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

points: If thou indeed obey his voice, I will be an enemy unto thine enemies and an adversary unto thine adversaries. These enemies are not the same enemy of verse four: the enemy of verse four is your brother whom you must help and shew mercy; these enemies in verse 22 the Lord himself deals with and destroys for you.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

points: The Angel goes before Israel unto the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites, to cut them off. Thou shalt not bow down to their gods nor serve them nor do after their works, but utterly overthrow them and quite break down their images.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

points: Serve the Lord your God, and he shall bless thy bread and thy water, take sickness away from the midst of thee, none casting their young nor barren in the land, and the number of thy days he will fulfil. He drives the nations out by little and little, lest the land become desolate and the beasts multiply, until Israel be increased and inherit the land.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

points: The bounds are set from the Red Sea even unto the sea of the Philistines, and from the desert unto the river, the river Euphrates. That little sliver on the map today is not how big Israel is supposed to be: the land was to encompass all the way out to the Euphrates by Babylon, taking in parts of what is Iraq and Iran, and it will be filled one day.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

points: Thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor with their gods. They shall not dwell in thy land, lest they make thee sin against me: for if thou serve their gods, it will surely be a snare unto thee. This is the third way the Lord states the command of verse 13 in this chapter: no learning their worship, no serving, no covenant.
